StoredSessionRepository.kt:52-55 removes session.consent and session.careerStage on signOut and clear. StoredSessionRepositoryTest.signOut_removesLegacySessionKeys and clear_removesLegacySessionKeys now assert both keys, so round-1 F3 is fixed. ApplicationCleanup.kt:18-19 and RoomLocalDataWiper.wipeAll (LocalDataWiper.kt:29-34: clearAllTables + store.clear) are unchanged. The account-delete path (DeleteAccountUseCase -> AccountWipeFinisher -> wipeAll) still clears everything. The new LegacyDataPurge (LegacyDataPurge.kt:9-13) removes only the coverletter. and prep.plan. prefixes. Every key that survives is under session., payment., usage., account., exports., reports.content., tailor.edited., tailor.regenerations. or tailoring.request., and none of these collides with the purged prefixes. A grep of every MockStateStore user in main, prod, demo and debug finds no production read or write of the purged prefixes other than ApplicationCleanup.remove, so the async start-task race does not matter. The purge is idempotent and safe on a fresh install: DataStore 1.1.7 DataStoreImpl.kt:336 writes only if the new data differs from the current data, so a no-op purge does no disk I/O. Round-1 F1 (prep.plan.analysis-draft-*) is closed in production by the start task, and LegacyDataPurgeTest asserts the draft key.

Note: DeleteMyDataUseCase has no production caller on revamp/w1-base or at this head because YourData is already removed on the base. So the start task is the only shipped path for this purge (finding 3).

findings.rule: Not lazy about error handling: an app-scope start task must not crash start-up. House pattern: FinishPendingAccountWipeUseCase.kt:22-32 and PurchaseRestorer.kt:33-39 catch Exception (and rethrow CancellationException) inside their app-scope launches.
findings.trigger: A user upgrades from a build that stored coverletter.<id> or prep.plan.<id> while device storage is full. On launch, scope.launch { purge() } runs on @ApplicationScope (CoroutineScopesModule.kt:27: SupervisorJob + Default, with no CoroutineExceptionHandler). The keys exist, so the edit is not a no-op. DataStoreImpl.writeData throws IOException (no space left), the exception reaches the thread's uncaught handler, and the process dies. The keys stay, so every later launch crashes the same way until the user frees storage. Without this task, the demo flavour does only DataStore reads at start, so it would launch.
findings.title: Legacy purge start task has no exception handling and can crash-loop the app on a failed DataStore write
findings.proof: LegacyDataPurgeStartTaskTest: pass a MockStateStore whose removeWithPrefix throws IOException and a TestScope with a CoroutineExceptionHandler that records exceptions. Call start(), then advanceUntilIdle, and assert that no exception reached the handler. The test fails at the head. Fix: wrap purge() in try/catch (rethrow CancellationException, ignore other exceptions so the next start retries).

findings.rule: Checklist item 1 and Constitution IV.1: the fix for round-1 F1 needs a test that fails if the fix is reverted. PendingWipeStartTaskTest is the house pattern for start tasks.
findings.trigger: DeleteMyDataUseCase has no production caller at the base or the head (git grep finds it only in its own file and test, because YourData was removed on revamp/w1-base). The only shipped path that removes prep.plan.analysis-draft-* is LegacyDataPurgeStartTask. Delete the LegacyDataPurgeBindings @IntoSet method or make start() a no-op, and every test still passes, while upgraders keep the draft prep plan and cover letters on the device.
